{"clause_id":"c002","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line incorporation of the UCC definition; nothing to construe on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 1.3 supplies the Article 9 tie-breaker and the \"Code\" definition supplies the jurisdiction, so the reference is coherent.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c003","reasoning_cat1":"Broad but conventional enumeration of who counts as an obligor; the terms used are themselves defined elsewhere.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Notes Receivable machinery in Sections 4.3, 6.2 and the Eligible Notes Receivable definition.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c004","reasoning_cat1":"Standard definitional language with an illustrative parenthetical; \"related services\" is mildly open-ended but bounded by the Bank Product Provider requirement.","reasoning_cat2":"Fits the Bank Product/Bank Product Obligations scheme in Sections 2.3(b) and 3.6 without tension.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c005","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference definition with no substantive content.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.4(c) does in fact create the term \"Additional Documents,\" so the cross-reference is accurate.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c006","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference; nothing ambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 2.1(a) creates the terms as stated.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.03},

{"clause_id":"c008","reasoning_cat1":"\"Control\" is defined circularly as the power to direct management \"whether through ownership of Stock, by contract, or otherwise,\" and the deemed-Affiliate rules apply only \"for purposes of\" two provisions, leaving reach contestable. {"clause_id":"c243","reasoning_cat1":"A fixed three-year term, followed by a right to terminate \"immediately and without notice\" that is nonetheless \"subject to any notice and cure rights otherwise provided by this Agreement\" — the two halves of the sentence pull against each other.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 9.1(c) also allows termination on an Event of Default and Section 8.2 supplies cure periods, so the interplay of immediate termination and cure rights must be worked out.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c244","reasoning_cat1":"The provision is a placeholder, but it is numbered \"3.4\" in the text, duplicating the preceding Term section's number.","reasoning_cat2":"Section headings and numbers are declared to be for convenience only by Section 16.2, which blunts the effect of the duplication.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c245","reasoning_cat1":"Clear statement that all Obligations accelerate on termination and that Liens survive until payment in full and commitments end.","reasoning_cat2":"It coordinates with Sections 3.4, 3.7 and the cash-collateralization concept in the Section 1.4 \"repayment in full\" gloss; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c246","reasoning_cat1":"A definite 30-day notice and pay-off mechanic, with the premium expressly required.","reasoning_cat2":"Because the Applicable Prepayment Premium is zero after the first anniversary, the premium requirement becomes formal only, a coherent if odd result.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c247","reasoning_cat1":"A liquidated-damages recital covering four very different termination events, including foreclosure and plan confirmation, with the premium payable only \"if applicable\" — an ambiguity about when it is applicable at all.","reasoning_cat2":"Read with the Applicable Prepayment Premium definition (zero after year one) and Section 3.6's automatic acceleration, the clause may have no operative content after the first anniversary.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c248","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional grant of security interest, closing with a flat prohibition: \"except for Permitted Dispositions, Borrowers ... shall have no authority, express or implied, to dispose of any item or portion of the Collateral.\"","reasoning_cat2":"That prohibition makes the Permitted Dispositions definition and the release mechanics in Section 4.9(b) the only exit from the collateral pool, so a dispute over a sale of Notes Receivable would be decided by reading these provisions together with Sections 7.3(c) and 7.4.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.32},
{"clause_id":"c249","reasoning_cat1":"Requires endorsement and delivery of Notes Receivable, sets a $250,000,000 floor with the soft rider \"otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender,\" and the final sentence reads \"If Event of Default has occurred,\" dropping the article.","reasoning_cat2":"It interlocks with Sections 3.1(t), 3.3(e), 6.16 and 8.17, and with Section 4.9's release mechanics that take notes back out of Lender's possession.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.22},

{"clause_id":"c252","reasoning_cat1":"Three-Business-Day notification and assignment duty for commercial tort claims; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Borrower Collateral clause (c) and Schedule 5.7(d).","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},

{"clause_id":"c254","reasoning_cat1":"Assignment of storage access rights exercisable only after an Event of Default; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 5.5's public warehouse proviso and Section 7.15.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
